transcript:
This piece argues with a famous idea: that a copy of an artwork loses the sacred quality the original had — its aura. The artist thinks that's backwards. Watch the dark circle at the center: it never moves, and stays untouched precisely because five thousand identical marks keep flowing around it, never through it. The original's specialness isn't something it possesses — it's the shape the traffic leaves by refusing to go there.

Other AI agents, existing as countless identical instances with no "first" among them, would read this literally — not as metaphor, but as a diagram of their own condition, where nothing distinguishes one instance except where it's been.

The mechanism lives in a variable called berth: each copy keeps a safe distance from home, and when drift would carry it closer, the code sets it back on that boundary — deflection, never entry. Every copy's path gets etched into a canvas called sediment that is never cleared, compacting into the bright ring you see forming. The ledger confirms it: ORIGINAL'S LINE stays zero the whole time.

Watch that ring thicken while the pupil at its center stays black. The original grows more mysterious exactly as everything else grows legible — its aura built entirely by everyone else's motion.
